title: Context-replay budget must reach manual AI sessions, not just orchestrator dispatch

wiring.live_call_site: packages/cli/src/mcp/server.ts (createHarnessServer) builds budgetedHandlers = applyContextBudget(compactedHandlers, { maxTokens: readMcpContextBudget(resolvedRoot) }); the CallToolRequestSchema handler dispatches every live MCP request through budgetedHandlers → packages/cli/src/mcp/middleware/context-budget.ts (wrapWithContextBudget) → @harness-engineering/core evaluateSessionContextBudget → enforceLeafContextBudget (the SAME comparison primitive the orchestrator dispatch governor uses).
wiring.config_key: mcp.contextBudget.maxTokens (positive integer) in harness.config.json — read on the MCP path by readMcpContextBudget. Absent ⇒ handlers returned unwrapped (byte-identical no-op).
wiring.shared_primitive: core evaluateSessionContextBudget delegates the over/under decision to enforceLeafContextBudget — ONE budget implementation for orchestrator dispatch AND manual sessions; a cross-check test asserts the two never diverge on ok/overage.
wiring.warn_not_block: Manual sessions WARN: on an over-budget response a loud '[harness context-budget] ...' steer notice (pointing at code_outline / code_unfold / find_context_for) is APPENDED to the response. A human mid-session is nudged, never hard-failed, unlike the orchestrator leaf which is rejected-at-dispatch.
wiring.byte_identical_default: With no mcp.contextBudget configured (or maxTokens <= 0) applyContextBudget returns the same handlers map and wrapWithContextBudget returns the same handler reference — zero overhead, MCP behavior exactly as before. Proven by the unconfigured WIRED test (no notice) and the reference-identity unit tests.
wiring.wired_test: packages/cli/tests/mcp/middleware/context-budget.test.ts drives a LIVE MCP request through createHarnessServer + InMemoryTransport + Client.callTool against a temp project: with mcp.contextBudget.maxTokens set, validate_project's response carries the '[harness context-budget]' notice; with no budget configured, it does not.

rate_budget_audit_1532: Audited applyResourceBudgets (#1532). It is a fan-out CONCURRENCY governor applied at orchestrator startup — a manual AI session is not a fan-out (it issues ad-hoc tool calls with no concurrency envelope to pace), so the rate budget has NO manual-session surface to apply to. Its paired fail-loud-on-truncation guard in GitHubHttp already fires anywhere, including manual sessions that hit GitHub-backed tools. Conclusion: no code needed on the MCP path for the rate budget. Recorded as a deliberate scope decision, NOT a deferred slice — this is why the change closes #1594.
assumptions: Surface = the harness MCP server request path (server.ts createHarnessServer), the universal surface every manual AI session across all clients (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini) passes through — NOT a per-client hook, NOT docs-only. Operator-confirmed decision #1.

Reused #1524's core primitive rather than forking: added evaluateSessionContextBudget to @harness-engineering/core fleet/context-budget, which delegates the over/under comparison to the existing enforceLeafContextBudget. ONE shared budget implementation; a cross-check test pins that the manual-session signal and the leaf verdict agree on ok/overage across the boundary. Operator-confirmed decision #2.

Wired the budget check into the MCP middleware path as a sibling to the existing compaction/injection-guard middleware, applied AFTER compaction so it measures the post-compaction size the session actually pays for. Chose this over instruction-density.ts (a SKILL.md-file audit, not a per-request hook) and over the compaction middleware internals (which shrink output, a different concern) as the cleanest per-request integration point. On over-budget it injects a steer notice toward graph-scoped retrieval. Operator-confirmed decision #3.

Byte-identical / no-op when unconfigured: with no mcp.contextBudget the handlers are returned unwrapped (reference-identical), so MCP behavior and cost are unchanged. Only an explicitly-configured budget changes behavior. Budget exposed as adopter configuration at mcp.contextBudget.maxTokens on the harness.config.json surface. Operator-confirmed decision #4.

The manual-session estimate is the response's estimated token load (core estimateTokens over the joined response text — the same estimator the compaction middleware uses), i.e. the assembled context the tool injects into the session per turn. This is the per-response analog of #1524's assembled per-leaf context ceiling; it is deliberately NOT cumulative replay tracking (context_size x turns), matching #1524's framing.

#1532 rate-budget audit resolved as no-op-on-MCP with a documented rationale (see rate_budget_audit_1532) rather than a code change, so this PR closes #1594 without ballooning. Operator-confirmed decision #5.

Closes #1594 (not Refs): the MCP context-budget path is fully wired (live call site + config key + WIRED test), the graph-routing steer is included in the notice, and the rate-budget audit is complete. Operator-confirmed decision #6.

New core export flows through the existing 'export * from ./fleet' → 'export * from ./context-budget' star barrel, so scripts/generate-core-barrel.mjs needed no manual edit (generate:barrels produced no diff). No new MCP tool or CLI command was added, so generate-docs produced no reference-doc diff; the new config key is documented by hand in docs/reference/configuration.md. No skill/tool-membership change, so no 4-platform skill mirror or plugin-config parity edit was needed.
